epic.title: data_mining: every fluoroscopy video dataset, solved one by one
epic.body: One issue per fluoroscopy video dataset of the Fluoroscopy Data Atlas (21 records of category fluoro_video in data_mining/data/datasets.json), each with its next step by status. tasks.title: Screen the Bern dynamic myelography videos on the grid
tasks.body:
Atlas record: **Bern dynamic myelography Videos 1-4 (Clin Neuroradiol 2021)** (`data_mining/data/datasets.json`, category fluoro_video).

- Status: held
- Grid path: /rs/rs_grp_oschome/go2432/data/external/fluoro_video
- Access: open download
- How to get it: PMC supplementary files of PMC8463391 (CC BY 4.0, with attribution).
- Licence: CC BY 4.0
- Link: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8463391/
- Size: 4 MP4s, 5-21 s each; pulsed 7.5 f/s, about 10-14 s per clip estimated from captions
- Notes: The closest public case to overlapping frames along one spine (the detector pans cranially with the contrast), but the step is not known and the web versions are re-encoded, cropped and have lost frame timing and geometry.

## What to do

Screen it on the grid: list every file under the grid path with its duration, frame rate, resolution and codec (ffprobe, in an sbatch job), and read the fluoro_video pipeline's clips.csv and REPORT.md for these files if the earlier run covered them (01_carm_level_detection/code/fluoro_video/README.md; the 1,269 extracted clips of the atlas record for the YouTube set); run the pipeline on them if it did not. Record for each file whether it holds live fluoroscopy or held frames, the view (AP, lateral), the levels in the field and any level named on screen.

Also measure, frame by frame, how far the field moves between frames where the detector pans cranially, so the step can be compared with the native DICOM that request letter 3 asks for.

## Done when

The dataset's source record in data_mining/data/sources/ is corrected with what was found (status, grid path, size, licence, notes), `python data_mining/scripts/merge_atlas.py` rebuilt datasets.json, the page and CATALOG.md, and the pull request says what the job ids and outputs were. Nothing of the frames goes into git.

Work it by docs/agents/PROTOCOL.md: a claim branch `claude/<this issue>`. Every computation is an sbatch job (root CLAUDE.md rule 7); no frame, video or patient data goes into git or to an outside AI service.
